Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:58 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's amazing how fast two weeks can change things. Louisville appeared to be ready to make a charge with a close loss to Ole Miss, a great 41-31 win over SMU, and winnable games coming up. A 30-27 loss to Wake Forest and a 31-28 loss to NC State later, and now the Cardinals have to win to stay alive in the ACC race. Florida State was done. Head coach Mike Norvell was all but fired, and then everything flipped. The Seminoles tuned up against Central Arkansas, and then stunned Virginia 38-7. Win this, and the season narrative totally changes. Florida State vs Louisville Quick Hits Florida State is on the road for four games in the next five, with a trip to Miami up next before hosting Clemson. Louisville goes to Syracuse next to start a run of three road games in four dates. Before the last meeting in the 2023 ACC Championship, the two teams split the previous ten games. How To Watch Florida State vs Louisville Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Game Time: 7:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville, KY – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Florida State Will Win So what did Florida State do against Virginia to generate all of this excitement? The defense pitched one of its best games in a long time, considering the circumstances, holding the Cavalier passing game in check with a monstrous day from the pass rush. The Noles generated ten sacks and 12 tackles for loss. The relentless pressure should continue against a Louisville offensive front that's having a problem keeping teams out of the backfield. Why Louisville Will Win Can Florida State show up on the road? It's not quite fair to dog the Noles for losing at Alabama, but the program has lost 13 straight games outside of Tallahassee, going back to the win over Florida late in 2023. Louisville has to take a deep breath after the NC State loss. It played well. The ground game was great, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz was fine on his dinged up ankle, and everything was fine outside of three lost fumbles. Florida State hasn't forced a takeaway in a month. Florida State vs Louisville Prediction, Betting Lines Florida State isn't awful. The pieces are there – the ground game is solid, and look out if that pass rush keeps on rolling – but they have a hard time always fitting together. The Seminoles will crank up plenty of yards and points – the Louisville defense isn't anything special – but the offense will stall a few too many times, and the Cardinals will find their offensive scoring punch after two straight disappointments. away.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. The Seminoles will be without four linebackers after the LaVallee announcement, as the freshman will join Izayia Williams, Blake Nichelson, and Daylen Green on the sidelines this week. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska Football vs. Indiana Preview & Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska is getting ready for a huge Big Ten matchup against Indiana, and Adam Carriker breaks down what the Huskers have to do if they want to pull off the upset and earn some serious respect. This is one of those games that can change the way people look at a team. Nebraska has put together a strong start, but now the Huskers get a chance to prove it against a ranked Indiana team led by Curt Cignetti. Indiana has been one of the best teams in the Big Ten, and this game will give Matt Rhule’s team a chance to show how far it has come. Carriker starts by looking back at the history between Nebraska and Indiana; he then shifts to Nebraska’s offense and quarterback Anthony Colandrea. If Nebraska is going to win this game, Colandrea will need to have a big day. He has to make smart decisions, take care of the football, and make plays with both his arm and his legs. Carriker also compares Colandrea to Indiana’s quarterback Josh Hoover and talks about why Nebraska needs to put pressure on Hoover and force him into mistakes. The Huskers’ pass catchers are another major part of the matchup. Nebraska has playmakers who can make a difference, and Carriker takes a closer look at players like Kwazi Gilmer and how they match up with Indiana’s defense. On the other side of the ball, Nebraska’s defense could be one of the biggest factors in the game. Rob Aurich and the Nebraska defense will need to be at their best, especially on third down. Indiana has talented receivers, solid running backs, and an offense that can hurt teams in several different ways. Nebraska cannot afford to give up easy conversions or big plays. One of the biggest topics in the episode is penalties. Nebraska had 16 penalties last week while Indiana had zero. That is a massive difference, and Carriker makes it clear that Nebraska cannot expect to beat a ranked team if it keeps hurting itself. Cleaning up the penalties is one of his biggest keys to the game. Carriker wraps up the show by laying out five keys for Nebraska: limit penalties, stop the run, play four full quarters, run the football, and limit big plays. None of those things are complicated, but Nebraska has to do all five if it wants to compete and win. The Huskers also need to be ready for a physical game. Carriker talks about trading blows with Indiana and matching the Hoosiers for all four quarters. This cannot be a game where Nebraska plays well for two or three quarters and then fades late. The second half will be huge. Carriker also throws in a little extra motivation with a beard bet if Nebraska wins. At the end of the show, he gives his final score prediction: Indiana 27, Nebraska 24. He sees it as a close game, but Nebraska will need a big performance from Colandrea, a strong game from the defense, and much cleaner football to pull off the upset. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! picks.blurb: 'We've Got to Play Extremely Hard': Nebraska Defensive Coordinator Rob Aurich Previews Indiana Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska gave up more yards to Maryland in the first quarter than it allowed against North Dakota the entire game. That won't be good enough against the Huskers' biggest test yet: the undefeated, defending national champions from Indiana . Rob Aurich knows it, too, and the Huskers' defensive coordinator says Saturday's contest will be decided by how well NU handles the little things, from players doing their jobs to tackling at a high level. Indiana's Turbo Richard runs for a touchdown against Western Kentucky. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Hoosiers' offense ranks 14th nationally, averaging 489.6 yards and 44.2 points per game. Aurich said some simple qualities will be key to slowing Indiana down. The Hoosiers' offense ranks 14th nationally, averaging 489.6 yards and 44.2 points per game. Aurich said some simple qualities will be key to slowing Indiana down. “Play style, speed, and physicality,” Aurich told reporters Tuesday. “Run to the ball. I thought two weeks ago we ran to the ball harder than we did last week. I was disappointed in that. I want people to talk about our defense as the hardest-playing group in the country. So, we’ve got to play extremely hard.” “The backs have a high break tackle ratio,” he continued. “We’ve got to tackle their backs at an elite level, which is something we’re going to work on today.” Anthony Jones Jr. makes a tackle against Michigan State. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Huskers allowed several explosive plays against the Terrapins last week, which is a major concern heading into a matchup against the likes of Indiana. The Huskers allowed several explosive plays against the Terrapins last week, which is a major concern heading into a matchup against the likes of Indiana. Aurich knows Nebraska won't be able to completely shut the Hoosiers down. But he does want to see the Huskers continue to bow up in the red zone, something they've been doing at a high level. Aurich mentioned Dwayne McDougle's game-changing 81-yard pick-six in the second quarter against Maryland. “He looked at that look all week, and so he had an opportunity to execute something he’s done" Aurich said. "I’ve been extremely pleased with our guys’ ability to toughen up in some big moments.” “I was really proud with how we survived that first half when things were a little noisy,” he continued. “I was really, really pleased with how they responded and we toughened up. And then obviously we went into halftime and had the ability to make the few corrections we needed to make and hold them low in the second half.” Josh Hoover celebrates after running for a touchdown against Northwestern. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With a touchdown-to-interception ratio of 15:0, Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover will try not to let the Huskers adjust. Outside of a close contest with Northwestern, he and the Hoosiers have essentially done whatever they've pleased. Outside of a close contest with Northwestern, he and the Hoosiers have essentially done whatever they've pleased. “He is operating their system,” Aurich said. “There’s a lot of stealing going on in the perimeter right now and he hasn’t forced a ton of throws. ... But yeah, he just hasn’t put the ball in harm's way yet.” With kickoff set for 11 a.m. CDT Saturday and the game televised by FOX, Husker fans will get to see how well the Big Red's defense stacks up. picks.blurb: Indiana vs. Nebraska score prediction by expert football model: Can the Huskers upset the champs? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Guardians-White Sox updates Dodgers-Braves updates Eagles-Ravens trade grades OBJ signs with Vikes Messi's Argentina farewell Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Matt Rhule has never defeated an AP top 25 ranked opponent while head coach at Nebraska, but this weekend will give him a perfect opportunity against college football's reigning national champion Indiana. And the Cornhuskers are off to a good start, coming in undefeated through five games, but still unranked and beating teams that are nothing like the caliber of opponent that they'll see this weekend in the Hoosiers and their 21-game win streak. What do experts think of this week's matchup? For that, let's turn to the SP+ college football model to project the outcome, and use it to lock in our own prediction. Indiana vs. Nebraska score prediction: Hoosiers have the road edge Sep 25, 2026; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Indiana Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover (10) throws a pass against the Northwestern Wildcats during the first half at Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Indiana remains the expected favorite against Nebraska on the road, but in what could be a close game. SP+ predicts that Indiana will defeat Nebraska by a projected score of 31 to 24 and will win the game by an expected margin of 7.7 points on the road. The model gives the Hoosiers a strong 69 percent chance of outright victory. SP+ is a "tempo- and opponent-adjusted measure of college football efficiency" that attempts to predict game outcomes by measuring "the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football." How good is it this season? So far, the SP+ college football prediction model is 146-122-3 in its picks against the spread with a 54.4 win percentage. What actually happens? Can the Huskers catch the Hoosiers? There's a lot to like about the Cornhuskers' offense right now. It ranks top 15 in points per game, scoring at least 31 in every game, and 48 in three out of five outings. Indiana hasn't looked its usual self until laying a 47-15 beating on Rutgers a week ago, and it still boasts one of the most potent rushing attacks in the country, tacking on 253 yards on the ground on average. Nebraska has performed admirably well against its competition thus far, but the discrepancy between what the Hoosiers put on the field compared to those other teams is too great to ignore. Home field keeps the Huskers in it for a while, but Indiana has the firepower to pull away by double digits. What happens? Indiana beats Nebraska and covers the spread. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 Mon, October 5, 2026 at 1:29 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College Football can be odd. One minute, you're winning your conference opener on the road 31-13. The next minute, you're winning you're conference home opener 48-25. You don't look particularly great in either contest, but you cover the spread, hold up your end of the bargain, and sit 5-0 to start the year for the first time since 2016. That's the story of the Nebraska Cornhuskers. LINCOLN, NE - OCTOBER 3: Nebraska defensive back Jeremiah Charles (25) celebrates after blocking a punt in the first quarter of the game between the Maryland Terrapins and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 3, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nebraska took care of the Maryland Terrapins, albeit with one of the more dysfunctional beginnings to a game you'll see. A penalty on a (nearly) blocked punt that extended Maryland's drive, resulting in a field goal. Then after a three-and-out, an actual blocked punt that resulted in a Mekhi Nelson touchdown, his first of two in the game. Nebraska trained as much as 16-7, but still led 28-23 heading into halftime. The third quarter was a checkers match of moving a piece at a time, far away from your opponent. But the Huskers scored two seconds into the fourth quarter, and added two more touchdowns before the game ended. Meanwhile, the Nebraska defense held the Terps scoreless and relatively impotent after the 8:54 mark of the second quarter. Now it is time for the Huskers' biggest (and some may say first true) test of the season when the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers make their way to Lincoln for Fox's Big Noon Kickoff. Curt Cignetti has his team in the top ten (top five in the Coaches' Poll), and even though there's no Fernando Mendoza, the Hoosiers are the only other team in the Bin ten to be undefeated. They have only been threatened once this year, when the Northwestern Wildcats of all teams gave them a scare, as the Hoosiers won that September 25 contest 29-23 at home. Indiana handled Rutgers this past weekend, and they mowed through their non-conference opponents (North Texas, Howard, and Western Kentucky) on easy mode. How will Nebraska perform against a rated team? Can they break the streak and knock off a ranked opponent? Would the rebuild fully be "on" if such a feat were to occur? Regardless of our collective thoughts on the outcome of the game, Vegas isn't counting on it. The line on FanDuel Sportsbook has Indiana as a 7.5-point favorite, marking the first time this season that Nebraska entered as the underdog. The over/under for the contest is 52.5 points. Bet your heart, but do so responsibly. Big Noon Kickoff between Nebraska and Indiana is Saturday at 11:00am Central, LIVE from Memorial Stadium, on Fox!

picks.headline: Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment
picks.blurb: Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Guardians-White Sox updates Dodgers-Braves updates Eagles-Ravens trade grades OBJ signs with Vikes Messi's Argentina farewell Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction: The Huskers' Big Moment Pete Fiutak Wed, October 7, 2026 at 6:51 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska enjoyed a few terrific seasons over the last 25 years, but for all intents and purposes, the historic superpower hasn't been in the national title hunt since losing to Miami in the BCS Championship to end the 2001 season. There's still plenty of work to do after this week, but beating the defending national champion – and putting an end to Indiana's 21-game winning streak – would be just the moment the program has been waiting for to show that it's headed in the right direction. Indiana hasn't been the dominant version of last year, but it's still unbeaten, it's about as tuned up as it can be, and it got its first road game out of the way with a 47-15 win over Rutgers. Yeah, this might be Nebraska's moment. It's also Curt Cignetti's moment to prove that for the Hoosiers, it's business as usual. Indiana vs Nebraska Quick Hits The Hoosiers get three home games in the next four after this, but Ohio State is up next, the road date is at Michigan, and then Minnesota and USC come to Bloomington. Nebraska goes on the road for three games in the next four dates, with a trip to Oregon before a week off to get ready for Washington. Indiana won 56-7 in 2024, but the Huskers are 6-1 in the series before that going back to a Hoosier win in 1959. How To Watch Indiana vs Nebraska Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Memorial Stadium, Lincoln, NE – Week 6 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Expert Picks: Week 6 Why Indiana Will Win As you'd expect from one of the best coached teams in all of sports, Indiana doesn't mess up. It has only turned the ball over once, it's third in the nation in fewest penalties, and no one does a better job of not putting itself in tough situations. It might not be that Nebraska needs to force mistakes and can win this straight up, but it has a way of pulling away in games, helped by the takeaways. On the flip side, the Huskers were flagged 16 times in the win over Maryland and have committed the most penalties of any Big Ten team so far. Why Nebraska Will Win The Hoosiers have only been stress-tested once in the 29-23 win over Northwestern, and that was partly because Wildcat quarterback Aidan Chiles was accurate with the passing game. Nebraska's Anthony Colandrea might not be Drew Brees, but he's hitting 66% of his passes with 13 touchdowns and just two picks. This has to be about the Nebraska offensive line, though. The Huskers are taking over games with the running game pushing until the dam breaks, and then games turn into routs. Indiana isn't Maryland or Bowling Green, but Michigan State is a tough-as-nails team that was the only team that held the Huskers to under 200 yards, and it still lost by 18. Indiana vs Nebraska Prediction, Betting Lines Can Nebraska get close to 40 carries? Part of the problem against Indiana is that teams have to give up on the run because it doesn't work. Only North Texas has been able to get past 66 yards this season, and it's also the only team that ran more than 35 times. North Texas also lost 52-16. The energy of the moment will carry the Huskers to a solid first half, but they won't be able to pull away. Eventually, the Nebraska run defense will start to buckle, the IU pass rush will get to Colandrea, and the hype for the Ohio State game will start about 30 seconds after the final gun. away.blurb: The No. 5 Hoosiers (4-0) are getting ready to travel out to Rutgers with their top four running backs all dealing with injuries. On Thursday night, Lee Beebe Jr.'s name unexpectedly popped up on the latest availability report. Beebe, who was listed as questionable, had a career-best performance against Northwestern with 203 rushing yards and a touchdown. With Turbo Richard suffering an ankle injury in the 29-23 win, Beebe had career-high 24 carries. The Hoosiers are optimistic about Richard's status for Saturday's game, but they have little depth at the position if either running back suffers a setback with Khobie Martin (arm) listed as out and Sean Cuono listed as questionable. The rest of IU's availability report remain unchanged from Wednesday. Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek .

away.headline: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers
away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. home.blurb: Rule was labeled as doubtful in NU's initial availability report Wednesday. He remained there Thursday before moving up to questionable Friday. His return would bolster a running back room with an alarmingly low amount of career production. After being upgraded from questionable to probable, he appears set to return against the Terps. That would give the Huskers a key piece in both their passing and return games. If he sits this one out, more catches could be in store for Quinn Clark and Keelan Smith. Isaiah Mozee and Andrew Marshall are options as punt returners. The surprising news came Thursday when junior running back Mekhi Nelson was added to the availability report as questionable. That status stayed the same on Friday. Nelson's availability would provide a significant boost for the Huskers on the ground against Maryland. With Jamal Rule also questionable, NU could enter Saturday's contest without their two most productive backs. Isaiah Mozee, listed as a co-No. 1 on the depth chart with Rule and Nelson, has 31 carries for 149 yards this season, plus three receptions for 37 yards. Backups Kwinten Ives, Vincent Genatone and Conor Booth have combined for 10 carries for 49 yards and three receptions for 38 yards. West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: West Virginia football expert previews the Arizona Wildcats game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 7, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football RichRod Week! It’s not just Game Week, it’s RichRod Game Week! Arizona’s first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod’s squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: “There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don’t think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn’t looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering.” It’s to no one’s surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What’s been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona’s defense will try to neutralize this? “We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn’t realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn’t what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games.” Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? “I think it’s fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don’t blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage.” The Mountaineers’ defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? “In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can’t get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It’s rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley’s reputation as a sort of ‘mad scientist’ on defense could be part of the problem. It’s really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn’t matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here.” How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? “After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I’ve seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod’s first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it’s humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn’t want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around.” Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. “We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. The Wildcats enter Saturday at 4-1 overall and 1-1 in Big 12 play after making a major statement with a 34-7 win over previously unbeaten Cincinnati. West Virginia, meanwhile, is 3-2 overall and still searching for its first conference victory after dropping back-to-back games against Oklahoma State and Iowa State. The Mountaineers' latest loss was a wild 45-42 shootout in Ames. There's also an obvious storyline on the West Virginia sideline, where former Arizona head coach Rich Rodriguez will face his old program. Rodriguez coached the Wildcats from 2012-17 before eventually returning to Morgantown for his second stint leading the Mountaineers. Can Arizona build off its impressive win over Cincinnati, or will West Virginia get its first Big 12 victory of the season at home? Here's everything you need to know about Arizona vs. West Virginia , including the latest odds, our biggest question and our prediction and pick for Saturday's Week 6 matchup. West Virginia vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Arizona -3.5 Over/Under: 61.5 Moneyline: Arizona -162/West Virginia +134 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Can West Virginia's Defense Stop Anything? This West Virginia defense is just horrible. They gave up 577 yards to Iowa State last week, and are allowing a Big 12-worst 456 yards per game, which is 50 more yards per game than any other Big 12 team. They're dead last in passing and rushing yards allowed per game, and second-worst in points allowed per game. The Mountaineers are 100th in the nation in net yards per play (offense minus defense), and rank dead last in defensive efficiency in the league. OK, you get the point. So what is Rich Rodriguez and Zac Alley changing ahead of Saturday? It's not clear. But something needs to change. West Virginia vs. Arizona Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 35, West Virginia 31 The West Virginia Mountaineers are going to be desperate to avoid an 0-3 start in Big 12 play. They have the running game to keep this thing competitive, however, Arizona's front seven is underrated. One week after Cincinnati rushed for over 200 yards vs. Kansas State, they only mustered 74 yards on 28 carries for 2.6 yards per carry vs. Arizona. I don't believe Arizona will have that level of success vs. this WVU rushing attack, that has been the most-potent in the Big 12, but they'll do enough. And if Arizona can jump out to a lead and force Michael Hawkins Jr. to try and win a game through the air, that's a recipe for success. The only concern I have for Arizona is the travel and early kick at 12:00 p.m. CT, which will be a 9:00 a.m. kick for Arizona's body clock. Those games are always tough. However, if you're worried you're on an island with Arizona, don't be. The Wildcats are attracting 91% of the money wagered and have been bet up from -3 to -3.5 , indicating that both recreational and larger bettors are backing Arizona. Sometimes the obvious side is obvious for a reason. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. UA coach Brent Brennan confirmed Monday that junior Tre Spivey will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a foot injury in Saturday's 34-7 win over Cincinnati. Brennan said Spivey will have surgery this week. The 6-foot-4, 215-pound Spivey was injured on Arizona's final offensive play of the first half and returned to the sidelines in the second half with a boot on his left foot. Spivey, in his second year with the Wildcats, leads the team with 22 receptions, 314 yards and four touchdowns. He had three catches for 36 yards prior to getting hurt.

Arizona WR Gio Richardson exits Cincinnati game after returning from injury Skip to main content SI.COM The Arizona Wildcats made it clear how valuable star wide receiver Gio Richardson is on Saturday against Cincinnati, going to him twice on the first drive of the game after the sophomore missed the last two games with a leg injury. But after hauling in two catches for 26 yards, Richardson went back into the locker room during the first drive - eventually returning to the sideline in shorts and without his helmet, a clear indication his night is done with less than five minutes of time off the clock. Richardson had a seven yard gain on first and ten to push Arizona across midfield, and hauled in a 19 yard gain two plays later to push the Wildcats to the 18-yard line. Running back Kedrick Reescano scored two plays later to give Arizona a 7-0 lead. Former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player Cody Jackson erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. Oct 3, 2026 Updated Oct 3, 2026 AMES — Cody Jackson transferred to Iowa State last winter in search of his fourth fresh start. The talented transfer wide receiver found it, but catches proved tough to come by. Until Saturday, when the former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. “I trusted in God, number one, and trusted in my coaches (and) my teammates,” said Jackson, who didn’t record a catch in ISU’s first two games, but now has 12 receptions in the past two games. “Not having my head down. Keeping my head high. Keeping a smile on my face every day and coming in and working at practice.” Jackson’s first grab on Saturday for the Cyclones (3-2, 1-1 Big 12) turned into a 46-yard touchdown on a halfback toss from Aiden Flora. His other seven receptions against the Mountaineers (3-3, 0-2) came during a tense second half, and many fueled three straight scoring drives that helped ISU preserve the win. “He did a great job finding open windows and attacking the ball in the air,” Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor said. Jackson notched 92 yards after the catch and often adjusted his routes as Raynor improvised amid amped up West Virginia pressure. His 43-yard catch on third-and-six early in the fourth quarter set up Kyle Konrardy’s 35-yard field goal that gave ISU a 31-28 lead. And Jackson’s 15-yard grab on the Cyclones’ final scoring drive ended in one of Flora’s three rushing touchdowns. Flora’s now averaging 8.1 yards per carry and has rushed for 600 yards and six touchdowns. “(He’s) a great leader,” Jackson said. “He can do everything, like you could see. away.headline: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense
away.blurb: Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Return of Jamauri McClure Brings Major Boost to Tulane Offense As they practiced on Tuesday for game prep coming off their bye week, Green Wave running back Jamauri McClure was a sight for sore eyes out there, participating in team drills without a non-contact jersey for the first time since he went down with a fractured foot in fall camp. This year's room looks a lot different in comparison. Maurice Turner is playing his best football right now. Jaylin Lucas has gotten some work out in space a bit more this week of prep. Johnnie Daniels has shown that he can throw a killer block as much as he can shoot through a gap. However, the return of McClure is what fans have been clamoring for since the news first got out that he was hurt. Now that he's had ample time to recover, his return should be a major boost for a Tulane offense looking to make the most out of and stretch out what should be expected to be limited possessions against the Army Black Knights Saturday. Messi's Argentina farewell (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Maddy Hudak Tue, October 6, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The best ability is often availability, and the Tulane Green Wave certainly have some good news on that front ahead of American conference play. But while head coach Will Hall told media members on Tuesday that he and the team feel that they're a better football team than when we last talked to and saw them last two weeks back, they have a lot to prove on the road to kick off their conference slate. An essential thing they're looking for is an identity on offense. Well, a lot of that can be solved by a strong rush attack that McClure instantaneously boosts. When McClure started taking over the starting running back job towards the end of the year last season, it was clear that he had a different gear and set of traits than what we were seeing from that room. Further good news on that front is that nothing appears to be up with Turner, who ended up limping a bit at the end of his 74-yard touchdown run against the Southern Miss Golden Eagles, as he also was practicing in full with no non-contact jersey. But the true finesse of that room lies with McClure. Another major returnee was wide receiver Zycarl Lewis, who got injured during the season opener against the Duke Blue Devils and hasn't practiced or played since. He was also not in a non-contact jersey on the practice field Tuesday. McClure averaged an impressive 6.5 yards per carry last season. The redshirt sophomore had eight total carries until Week 12 of last year against the FAU Owls. In the final five games of the season, he added 75 touches for 83 total carries for 540 yards and two touchdowns.

away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: News Sports Life Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLLEGE Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane Ken McMillan Middletown Times Herald- Record Updated Oct. 6, 2026, 9:47 a.m. ET In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset
picks.blurb: No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma preview: Reeling Sooners look to pull off upset | Burnt Orange Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Texas Longhorns Community Burnt Orange Nation October 7, 2026 Burnt Orange Nation Notifications Notifications Get The App Sections Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Texas Football Odds Texas Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search Get The App Sections Expand Texas Longhorns Recruiting Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications Texas Longhorns Football The Sooners head to Dallas with a struggling offense and stingy defense. Fresh off a bye week with a 4-0 record, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns head up I-35 for the annual Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners, who have struggled thus far in 2026 — Oklahoma has a 2-2 record on the year and has failed to score more than 14 points in each of their last three contests. On paper, this is a matchup that should favor the Longhorns, but if history has shown anything, nothing matters once these two teams take the field at the Cotton Bowl. Scoring points against the Oklahoma defense is doable but will undoubtedly be the biggest challenge facing the Longhorns. “This is always a unique game because you can take record, stats, and all those things and throw them out the window,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. “You’ve got to play the game and you’ve got to play the game the right way.” The struggles for the Sooners start on the offensive end. Returning quarterback John Mateer has failed to effectively move the ball through the air and the running attack ranks 131st in the FBS in yards per game. Second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle has made his money with Mateer at the helm, a partnership that is now in it’s fourth year and dates back to their time together at Washington State, but is currently testing the patience of Oklahoma fans given the offense’s lack of scoring. “Coach Venables, I know he’s probably sitting there thinking he wishes the record was a little bit different, but man, his teams play hard, and this team’s no different,” Sarkisian said. “They play hard. They’re an excellent defensive football team. They’ve got draft picks all over on the defense. Offensively, they’ve got playmaking ability similar to us. They’re trying to find their way to to find that level of consistency. But one thing I can be assured of — we’re going to get their best shot, and so I think it’s important for us that we focus on what we need to do so that we can play our best football.” With concerns across the Sooner offense, this year’s rendition will likely be determined by the success of the Longhorns finding the end zone in the Cotton Bowl. If the Longhorns can score points, things could get out of hand. Here’s what to expect on Saturday. As mentioned, the Oklahoma offense is headed by Arbuckle and Mateer. Arbuckle is a young and forward-thinking coordinator with a track record of quarterback development and roots in the Air Raid. At 31 years old, he has already helped develop Bailey Zappe, Austin Reed, and Cam Ward. His offense utilizes tempo and the run game to stretch defenses and create passing windows. With the athleticism of Mateer and the inability to create an impactful rushing attack otherwise, Arbuckle has adapted the offense to feature a quarterback run threat on nearly every play. Averaging just 22 points per game and coming off a bye week, a few new wrinkles are all but guaranteed from Arbuckle on Saturday. Much has been made of Mateer’s play at quarterback this season. The returning starter for the Sooners came into the season with lofty expectations after a turnover-prone 2025 season. Through four games, his play has been disappointing, prompting Venables to admit that he considered benching his starting quarterback at halftime of the Georgia loss. Mateer has completed 66.1 percent of his passes for 883 yards and eight touchdowns while adding 41 carries for 76 yards. However, Mateer has turned the ball over six times in four games, including three first-half turnovers last week against Georgia. Pro Football Focus has tracked eight throws by Mateer as turnover worthy this season. Holding on to the ball is priority number one for Mateer, who has looked rattled in the pocket the season. He’s missed reads, held on to the ball, and fired inaccurately on numerous occasions. Keeping Mateer uncomfortable sets the tone for the Texas defense. Nearly everything else is downstream of whether the Longhorn front can keep him guessing and rushed. Keeping Mateer’s legs out of the game will be another key for Texas — if Mateer can extend plays or effectively pick up first downs on designed runs, things get significantly more complicated for the Longhorn defense. Expect a heavy dose of quick, high-completion throws to start the game in order to neutralize the Texas pass rush and get Mateer into a rhythm. The lead back for the Sooners is junior Lloyd Avant. Avant is a 5’10, 212-pound ball carrier from Humble who has racked up 164 yards and a touchdown on 42 carries (3.9 YPC). A transfer from Colorado State, Avant was expected to compete for snaps with Tory Blaylock, but has been thrust into the starting role due to Blaylock’s hamstring injury. Against UTEP, Avant looked strong, rushing for 79 yards on 15 carries; however, in the three games since, he has carried the ball 27 times for just 85 yards. Blaylock came into the season as the leading back, but is recovering from injury. He’s gotten a handful of carries, but its clear that the coaching staff does have not believe he is close to 100 percent. With an additional week to recover, it’s very possible that he contributes in a more meaningful way on Saturday. Regardless of who takes handoffs, improvement is needed on the ground. After finishing 113th in rushing offense last season, the Sooners are 133rd in yards per rush and t-134th with two rushing touchdowns on the season. Despite an offseason of revamping the rushing attack, things have regressed through four games. “It’s frustrating because I feel like I’m not doing my part,” said tight end Rocky Beers , via OU Insider . “There’s always one miss here, one miss there, and it’s costing us... We’ve just got to believe in our blocks and hold onto them as long as we can.” Getting back to running the ball was undoubtedly a point of emphasis over the bye week and something that the Longhorns will need to thwart on Saturday. Wide receiver Perhaps the most talented player on the Sooner offense is leading wide receiver Isaiah Sategna. A transfer from Arkansas, Sategna leads the offense in receptions (20), yards (267), and longest play from scrimmage (53). His two touchdowns are tied for the most on the team. Listed at 5’10, Sategna isn’t a huge target but can be dangerous. His quickness can generate missed tackles and additional yardage after the catch, so closing in quickly will be important come Saturday. Sategna forced 22 missed tackles last season and half of his receiving yards this season have come after the catch. Transfers Trell Harris and Parker Livingstone were brought in to supplement Sategna but neither has been effective thus far. Harris remains sidelined with an injury and Livingstone hasn’t been able to make a difference, though this will undoubtedly be a big game for him after transferring from Texas during the offseason. Stopping Sategna will be the key to keeping the wide outs locked down, a task that Longhorns defensive coordinator Will Muschamp has to feel good about. Veteran tight end Rocky Beers, a Colorado State transfer, has proved to be a reliable weapon for Mateer in the passing game, tallying 18 catches for 255 yards and two touchdowns this season, which is the best on the team outside of Sategna. One of three tight ends brought in from the portal by new position coach Jason Witten, Beers has looked the part this season. His route running creates windows for Mateer and he has enough size to be a matchup problem on smaller defenders. When Oklahoma makes it to the red zone, Beers is a frequent target, something that Texas will need to take away come Saturday. Offensive line The running game has struggled for the Sooners and a big reason for that falls on the shoulders of the offensive line. This group has failed to keep a clean pocket, generate push, and open running lanes. If Oklahoma hopes to turn things around offensively, the five up front will need to step up their performance, immediately. Against Georgia, the Oklahoma offensive line switched things up, sitting Eddy Pierre-Louis at guard in favor of Heath Ozaeta and Noah Best, but it made little difference. E’Marion Harris, the right tackle, still looked a step slow while star left tackle Michael Fasusi remains sidelined with a shoulder injury. I’d expect this group to get additional help in blocking from tight ends and running backs, as well as a heavy dose of plays designed to get the ball out of Mateer’s hand quickly. This group has yet to show anything special through four games, increasing pressure on longtime position coach Bill Bedenbaugh, whose tenure dates to the Bob Stoops era. The Oklahoma offense has sputtered to start the year. Poor quarterback play coupled with a lack of rushing attack and porous offensive line has resulted in little points being scored. With a bye week to prepare for the Longhorns, I’d expect a sharpened game plan out of the gate that features quick passes and unique ways to get the ball out of Mateer’s hands. For the Longhorn defense to find success, getting pressure is key. When Mateer feels the pass rush, he has shown an inability to make good reads and deliver accurate passes. Keeping him from feeling comfortable will be a point of emphasis for the Longhorns. Outside of Mateer, limiting Sategna and Beers is the next priority. Forcing someone besides these three players to make a difference should spell success for the Longhorns. For every concern about the offense, the defense boasts a strength. This unit has been salty thanks to a solid crop of returners despite a mediocre offense on the other side of the ball that can’t finish drives and turns the ball over. Moving the ball through the air against the Sooners has been particularly tough. Allowing 122.5 passing yards per game, the OU secondary ranks fourth in the country, and is led by returning producers that understand the scheme and have the physical talent to implement it successfully. Opponents convert 23.1 percent of third downs, the third best in the entire country, meaning staying ahead of the chains will be essential for the Texas offense. The best method to attack this defense has been via the run. Averaging 115.5 yards per game on the ground and 3.23 yards per carry, this aspect remains in the top third of the country but lags behind the stellar pass and third-down defense. Don’t be mistaken by the record or score against Georgia — the Oklahoma defense can get after it. Defensive line Up front, there are four players that Texas will need to handle — defensive ends Taylor Wein and Adepoju Adebawore, and tackles David Stone and Jayden Jackson. In the middle, Stone and Jackson are a formidable duo. Stone was one of the Sooners’ most highly-regarded returners after notching 43 tackles a year ago. Now in his third year at Oklahoma, the 6’3, 312-pound lineman will be looking for his first win in Dallas. Next to him, Jackson is quite the player. Last season, he tallied 28 tackles and 3.0 sacks, including being honored as the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week for his performance against Auburn. This duo up front has been a big reason why the defense has been stout thus far. picks.blurb: Early odds have Texas and Oklahoma in a total slugfest, with Horns coming out on top Skip to main content Recruiting Women's sports Men's Basketball Women's basketball Softball and Baseball Texas Longhorns history FanSided NCAA Sites Finally, and I mean finally, it is time to see if the Texas Longhorns can hold the Oklahoma Sooners touchdown-less for a third season in a row. As of today, it has been 1,094 days since OU reached the end zone, dating back to the Sooners' 2023 upset (fluke) win over the Horns. However, even as Texas has held Oklahoma to just three field goals over the last two Red River Rivalries, the Longhorns haven't exactly put on offensive showcases . This year, the expectations for the offenses aren't all that different, and the oddsmakers have the 2026 Red River Rivalry as low-scoring as the last couple of seasons. But don't worry, they still have the Horns coming out on top. Early odds for No. 1 Texas vs. Oklahoma in Red River Rivalry Spread: -7.5 Texas, +7.5 Oklahoma Moneyline: -330 Texas, +260 Oklahoma Over/Under: +/-39.5 points While the oddsmakers have Texas walking away with a victory by more than a touchdown, they also have the point total set below 40 points between the two teams. In other words, they expect the final score to be somewhere around 23-16 or 24-16, seemingly alluding to the idea that the Sooners will be able to find the end zone in the Cotton Bowl, a first in nearly 1,100 days by the time the game kicks off on Saturday. The moneyline favors Texas a little more heavily, with someone having to bet $330 on the Horns just to profit $100, but only having to wager $100 on Oklahoma to walk away with a $260 profit. Odds are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook . Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. If you ask me, 16 points is way too high a score for an OU offense that has looked even worse than it did over the last two years, especially when you consider how dominant the Texas defense was through the first four games. The Horns have allowed just 13.3 points per game so far this season, and that includes matchups against the then-No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes and then-No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers. Meanwhile, in Oklahoma's only Power Conference games (losses to the then-unranked Michigan Wolverines and No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs), the Sooners have only averaged 11.5 points per game, and most of that is coming from the defense or special teams. Also read: 3 weaknesses in Oklahoma's game that Texas must exploit in Red River Rivalry On the other side of the ball, Texas's point total almost entirely relies on 1) the offensive line's ability to maintain protection and 2) quarterback Arch Manning's ability to make the right decisions. Yes, the Horns obviously need to get the run game going again, but Manning's level of play seems to determine how well Texas performs on offense. Texas and Oklahoma are scheduled to kick off at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Oct. 10, and the game will be broadcast on ABC. Texas, still the class of the SEC , owns signature wins against Ohio State and Tennessee that catapulted it into the top AP ranking. Oklahoma fell out of the poll after falling to 2-2 and is once again facing structural questions around what remains a very anemic offense. away.blurb: Well, this week's message is along that exact same vein, with the Horns' head coach denying to provide any additional context ahead of releasing the first availability report of the week, which comes out at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday evening. Both were listed as "OUT" on the final availability report for Week 4 , alongside defensive back Xavier Filsaime and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman. For now, one could hope (and reasonably assume, based on Sarkisian's message about getting healthier) that at least one of those players is ready for, or close to ready for, action in the rivalry game. Texas gives injury non-update on Hollywood Smothers, Nick Townsend status once again Skip to main content Recruiting After nearly a week and a half since we last saw the Texas Longhorns take the field against the Tennessee Volunteers, many people were eager to hear how previously injured players had progressed over the bye. However, what should come as no surprise is that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had another idea in mind : no update. With star players like running back Hollywood Smothers, tight end Nick Townsend, and defensive lineman Justus Terry all missing time this season, Longhorn Nation has been eager to see their guys back in action. Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see what we should expect on Saturday. "I think we're healthier than we were a week ago at this time," Sarkisian said in his game preview press conference, continuing his refusal to share injury updates beyond what he puts in the SEC-mandated availability reports. Steve Sarkisian sticks to SEC availability report and nothing more On Monday of Week 4, before the Horns faced the Vols, Sarkisian expressed a similar sentiment, refusing to update members of the media on any lingering injuries, stating that "There's called an injury report in the SEC, so that's enough of the injury questions," Sarkisian said that week. Based on the final injury list from Texas's game against Tennessee, one could easily assume that Smothers will be good to go against the Oklahoma Sooners this weekend as the Horns prepare for the annual Red River Rivalry. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. home.blurb: Defensive tackle Justus Terry, defensive back Xavier Filsaime and offensive lineman Jordan Coleman were all unavailable against Tennessee, while tight end Nick Townsend had been listed as doubtful. Texas Injuries Could Shape Red River Matchup Against Oklahoma LonghornsRoundtable 446 Members • 1,685 Posts LonghornsRoundtable LonghornsRoundtable Related stories Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Texas Injuries Could Shape Red River Matchup Against Oklahoma Timothy Hamm Partner Oct 4, 2026 6:14 PM Published Oct 4, 2026 6:14 PM Texas enters Oklahoma week healthier after its bye, but several key Longhorns remain worth watching ahead of Saturday’s Red River Rivalry in Dallas. More Videos Texas football enters Red River Rivalry week in a better injury position than it faced at Tennessee, but the Longhorns still have several important availability questions before Saturday’s showdown with Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl. The biggest positive involves running back Hollywood Smothers, who missed the Tennessee game despite dressing in an emergency role. MORE: Ex Texas Star Wins NFL Rookie Honor Steve Sarkisian indicated after the 20-17 win that Smothers was close enough to play if absolutely necessary. The following bye week gave Texas additional time to get its leading rusher healthy. That could matter considerably against Oklahoma. Smothers leads Texas with 198 rushing yards on 41 carries and gives the Longhorns another physical option alongside Raleek Brown and Derrek Cooper. Texas managed without him at Tennessee, but getting Smothers back would make life considerably easier for quarterback Arch Manning. Wide receiver Cam Coleman also appears to be trending toward full availability after suffering a bruised tailbone against Tennessee. Coleman returned to that game, and Sarkisian described the injury as nothing serious. His presence opposite Ryan Wingo is important because Texas needs its vertical passing game intact against an Oklahoma defense likely to challenge Manning with pressure and disguised coverages. The bigger uncertainty may be on defense. Terry’s status could be particularly important. Oklahoma’s offense will test Texas between the tackles, and having another disruptive interior lineman would allow the Longhorns to keep their defensive front fresh while freeing star edge rusher Colin Simmons to attack the quarterback. Simmons dealt with wrist and elbow discomfort against Tennessee but returned to the game and is not currently expected to miss Oklahoma. MORE: Texas Longhorns Visit 5-Star WR Commit Amid Bye Week, Flip Buzz Texas is 4-0 and ranked No. 1 entering Saturday’s 2:30 p.m. CT matchup in Dallas. The Longhorns have won the past two Red River meetings by a combined 57-9, including a 23-6 victory last season. Still, rivalry games rarely follow the script.

Stone figures to be a big key in helping the Sooners slow down the Longhorns' running game Saturday. | Carson Field, Sooners On SI Ryan Aber Tue, October 6, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads NORMAN -A smile flashed across David Stone 's face when the Oklahoma defensive tackle was asked after Monday's practice how he felt. "I feel good, man," Stone said. " The bye week did justice for me, so I'm ready." Exactly two weeks earlier, Stone was unsure whether he'd ever play football again, much less be ready to play in the Red River Shootout. A dislocated kneecap, which Stone suffered in practice Oct. 21, certainly isn't a minor injury but the junior avoided major structural damage and was able to play five days later in the Sooners' 41-13 loss to No. 2 Georgia. If Oklahoma is to pull off an upset over top-ranked Texas on Saturday in the Cotton Bowl , Stone figures to need to be a centerpiece of the defensive attack. The team that wins the rushing battle generally wins the OU-Texas game over the past quarter century. And while it would be a surprise if the Sooners put up big rushing numbers on offense - they're averaging fewer than 100 yards per game on the ground and just 75.3 over the last three. The defense, though, has been strong against the run so far. They haven't allowed more than 152 yards on the ground this season and haven't allowed 200 rushing yards in any game since the 2024 Armed Forces Bowl. Stone performed well against the Bulldogs even though he was just a few days removed from the injury. He was happy for the bye week after that loss. "I very much needed it, honestly," Stone said of the bye week between Georgia and Texas. "I'm grateful that I had the time off to try to get my feet back under myself, especially my leg.It's just -it was bad. "I'm just grateful to play football again, honestly." Now, the Del City product will face the Longhorns for the third time in his career. Stone certainly has an appreciation for the rivalry. "As an Oklahoman, this is a game that you see growing up pretty much everywhere," Stone said. "The store you go to, you see the brands, the logos, of both schools across Texas and Oklahoma." Sep 5, 2026; Berkeley, California, USA; UCLA Bruins head coach Bob Chesney yells during the second quarter against the California Golden Bears at California Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dan Lanning Compares UCLA to Last Year's Indiana Dan Lanning Compares UCLA to Last Year's Indiana When speaking to the media back on Sept. 30, Lanning was quick to talk about the similarities that he has seen from the Bruins to last season's Big Ten and national champion, the Indiana Hoosiers. “They got some players that can play ball. Their running backs are as good as anyone who will go against them this year. They have a lot of players that came with them. And again, why I draw some comparisons to Indiana: a lot of guys that traveled with their coach right to the next stop.” First-year UCLA coach Bob Chesney brought offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy, defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler, and fifth-year running back Wayne Knight along with him to sunny California after the James Madison Dukes of the Sun Belt Conference made the College Football Playoff last season. Their memorable run came to an end in the first round after a 51-34 loss to the Ducks in the Pacific Northwest on Dec. 21, 2025. “Extremely well-coached team," Lanning continued on about this year's Bruins. "You got two coordinators who were with him before, so they've been together for a while. They have a lot of continuity from that standpoint. They're running the ball as well as anybody in college football.” Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Lanning Prepares to Deal With UCLA's Ground Game Lanning Prepares to Deal With UCLA's Ground Game Where the Ducks' defense needs to improve, in Lanning's mind, is in stopping explosive plays from UCLA's running barrage. Even the challenges that senior Nico Iamaleava presents through his aggressiveness on quarterback scrambles. On Oct. 5, Lanning reiterated to the media just how effective Chesney's offense is without an efficient passing game. "I would argue they have explosive runs; anytime you can run the ball in the end zone, I think they have more rushing touchdowns this year than they've had in the last two years combined," stated Lanning. Knight is one of the top ball carriers in the nation. He has already collected 445 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns (tied for the third-most in the sport). Slowing the star back down is the key to an Oregon winning effort over that confident unit in the backfield. "Against the run, I think we do a good job stopping runs between the tackles," Lanning explained back on Sept. 30. "However, we give up some big runs around the outside, and we need to do a better job defending and adjusting to those plays."
