picks.headline: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown
picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Guardians-White Sox updates Dodgers-Braves updates Eagles-Ravens trade grades OBJ signs with Vikes Messi's Argentina farewell Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. Six different Bruins have an interception, led by Ta’Shawn James with three, and UCLA is tied for the conference lead with five forced fumbles. The Bruins also have plenty of motivation. First-year coach Bob Chesney brought his James Madison team to Autzen last season and lost 51-34 after falling behind 34-6 at halftime. Ten former Dukes are on his first UCLA roster. picks.headline: 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks for ranked win vs. UCLA
picks.blurb: News Sports Opinion Entertainment Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL 4 bold predictions as Oregon football looks for ranked win vs. UCLA Alec Dietz Eugene Register-Guard Updated Oct. 7, 2026, 12:40 p.m. PT Just two weeks following an emotional, gut-check win over USC in Los Angeles, the Oregon football team will look to take down UCLA on Oct. 10 in Eugene . The Ducks (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) were idle last week in their only bye of the season and take on a Bruins ' (4-0, 2-0) squad in the same position. "UCLA is playing a high level of ball," coach Dan Lanning said. "It's a coaching staff that we have a really high level of respect for." The game will kick off at 12:30 p.m. Saturday and air on CBS. Here's what to look for ahead of the ranked matchup. Oregon vs. UCLA scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks are the only team in the country to average over 300 passing yards per game without an interception, split between starter Dante Moore and backup Dylan Raiola. Oregon ranks third nationally in passing yards per game and has done a good job of avoiding turnovers. If the Ducks can dictate tempo through the air, create explosive plays and avoid turnovers, they should win this game. Why UCLA has an advantage: The Bruins, to this point in the season, have run the ball much more consistently than the Ducks. UCLA ranks in the top five nationally in rush yards per play, rushing touchdowns and rushing yards per game. Led by standout back Wayne Knight, the Bruins average nearly 7 yards per carry. The Ducks rank toward the back half in the country around 4.6 yards per rushing attempt. If the Bruins can establish their ground game and control the tempo of this game, they'll have a chance to spring an upset. Oregon vs. UCLA injury updates For Oregon: The main storyline for the Ducks this week will likely be the health of starting quarterback. After suffering a concussion against USC, Moore returned to practice this week, but his status moving forward is unclear. Oregon's first mandatory injury report will be released Wednesday night and should offer clarity on his availability moving forward. Elsewhere, receiver Jeremiah McClellan is expected to be out still while Jalen Lott could make his return after a hand surgery sidelined him through Oregon's first four games. For UCLA: The Bruins' injury report will also be released Wednesday night, but several banged-up players made their returns in UCLA's last outing against Maryland in Week 4. Receiver Aidan Mizell, DB Jhase McMillan and tight end Josh Phifer were all listed as questionable or probable and shifted to available on game day. Safety Tao Johnson, a starter, could make his return after an upper-body injury in Week 1. Oregon vs. UCLA: 4 bold predictions Oregon needs to run the ball, much better than it has, to win Outside of a record-breaking outing against a completely outclassed opponent in Portland State, the Ducks haven't run the ball nearly as well as they typically have under Lanning. If you take out Oregon's 84-0 win over PSU, it is only rushing for roughly 115 yards per game, which would rank near the bottom of the country. The Bruins are one of the top rushing teams in the country. Though Oregon's offense has been able to move the ball effectively through the air, it will absolutely need to run the ball better than it has to beat the Bruins. Quarterback play will determine winner Through four games, Oregon's quarterback play has not been a major issue. Moore has been effective and avoided turnovers while Raiola stepped in masterfully to deliver a satisfying win over USC. That, obviously, needs to continue this Saturday, but the play of UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava might just determine how this game plays out. The previously maligned former five-star quarterback had a season to forget in 2025 but has been more effective in 2026. Still, the emphasis for Oregon all week will be on stopping the run, meaning Iamaleava will have opportunities to make plays throughout the game. If he can take advantage and outduel whoever starts at QB for Oregon, UCLA will be in the driver's seat to win. Oregon will play its best game of the season vs. UCLA Though the Ducks are 3-1, Lanning himself admitted during the bye week that they are nowhere near where they want to be. USC was a big step forward in multiple facets, but the defense has some lingering issues and the offense still has things to figure out. Saturday's game will be Oregon's best effort of the season, following a recalibrating bye week. Still feeling the urgency from the Oklahoma State loss in Week 2, getting back in front of fans at Autzen Stadium will energize the Ducks, who will roar out to a double-digit win this Saturday in Eugene. home.headline: Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable'
home.blurb: The Bears (2-3, 1-1 ACC) return home Saturday to face Virginia Tech (3-2, 1-1) in a 12:30 p.m. kickoff at Memorial Stadium. Will JKS miss his first game in two seasons or could he return to face the Hokies? We don’t know. Turns out Sagapolutele continued to show “some symptoms” during the second half and he now is among four Cal players undergoing multiple tests every day as part of the Bears’ concussion protocol program. Safety Kingston Lopa is also facing those protocols, Lupoi said. Besides Lopa going out with the head injury, the Bears played portions of the UNLV game without defensive backs Cam Sidney and Daniel Harris, both ejected after targeting penalties. Cal GM Ron Rivera on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele Injury vs. UNLV: It Was `Avoidable' Skip to main content SI.COM Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is among 10 Cal starters dealing with injuries — one of four in concussion protocol — coach Tosh Lupoi reported Tuesday. Cal is not required to provide details about injuries, although we will get status updates when the ACC releases its initial player availability chart on Wednesday night. We do know this much: Cal football athletic director and general manager Ron Rivera was not happy with the play that led to Sagapolutele leaving the game in the final minute of the half at UNLV. Rivera called the injury “avoidable.” Cal was trailing 24-7 when JKS rolled right and threw incomplete on first-and-10 from his own 25-yard line. UNLV linebacker Elias Rudolph, a transfer from Miami, flung Sagapolute to the artificial turf and the sophomore QB’s head bounced off the artificial turf. No flag was thrown, but Rivera clearly believed that should have happened. “JKS’s concussion, in my opinion, was avoidable. And I agree with Tosh, something should have happened,” he said. “When the quarterback throws the ball and the defender sees him throw the ball, there’s no reason to allow him to violently grab a guy and swirl around him and throw him to the ground. "Just go back and watch the tape. That’s all I’m going to say about that.” Lupoi removed Sagapolutele from the game after watching him stagger back to the huddle. At halftime, he was told JKS was cleared to play, but Lupoi said he didn’t feel comfortable sending him back onto the field. With backup Jackson Brousseau performing well at quarterback, Cal rallied to take a 25-24 lead in the second half before the Rebels answered to win 39-31. The closest Lupoi came to providing a hint as to whether Sagapolutele might face Virginia Tech was when he offered, “He was cleared to go back in at one point. That tells you it was a minor whatever-you-want-to-call-it.” Cal already has been playing without injured running backs Adam Mohammed and Carter Vargas. The Bears were desperate enough at the position that wide receivers Tyree Sams and Carson Perry-Smith were given snaps — and carries — at running back in Saturday. “You may or may not see that this week,” Lupoi said. home.blurb: Cal was without quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for the entire second half after he left the game in the final minute of the second quarter when he hit his head hard on the turf. He reportedly was cleared to return but Cal opted not put him back in the game with a head injury. Cal safety Kingston Lopa left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter and did not return. Bears starting nickel back Cam Sidney was ejected from the game for targeting in the first quarter. Cal defensive back Daniel Harris was ejected for targeting in the fourth quarter. INDIVIDUAL STAT OF THE GAME II: Cal limited all-Mountain West running back Jai'Den "Jet" Thomas to 46 yards on 16 carries. This game was considered a tipping point for Cal’s season, and it tipped the wrong way. Cal’s second straight loss reduces Cal’s chances to finish the season with a winning record for the second straight season. Before the season began, a 4-1 Cal record after five games seemed possible and a 5-0 start was not out of the question. A 2-3 mark at this stage was not what Cal supporters had in mind. The Bears have little momentum heading into the heart of its ACC schedule, which starts next Saturday with a home game against Virginia Tech. The outside complaints from Cal fans will continue, and the Bears are on the verge of becoming irrelevant this season. Cal rallied from a 24-7 halftime deficit to take the lead, but ultimately the Bears lost to UNLV 39-31 on Saturday afternoon at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Jackson Brousseau was the Bears' quarterback in the second half. Cal played the game without injured running back Adam Mohammed, the team’s leading rusher with 336 yards. RECORDS: CAL (2-3, 1-1 ACC), UNLV (3-2, 1-0 Mountain West) UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold. With Cal leading 25-24, UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold ran 42 yards to the Cal 12-yard line, which led to Arnold's 10-yard touchdown pass for a 32-25 UNLV lead with 9:38 left. KEY PLAY 1: On a fourth-and-2 play from the UNLV 47-yard line, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed a pass to Tyree Sams, but it was a half-yard short of a first down. It turned the ball over the UNLV with 12:20 left in the first quarter with the game scoreless. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings CBS Sports experts Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer reveal their final picks for college football's best games of Week 6, highlighted by an epic SEC clash Getty Images There are a couple of teams with considerable College Football Playoff résumé-strengthening opportunities this weekend, none bigger than a pair of nationally ranked matchups pitting title contenders from the SEC and Big Ten. Second-ranked Georgia 's trip to No. 6 Alabama should bring high drama between two unbeatens, along with No. 13 Oregon 's tussle at home with No. 21 UCLA , two squads trying to claw their way closer to Ohio State and Indiana at the top of the Big Ten hierarchy. Sorting through the contenders, potential upsets and matchups that look considerably trickier than the betting lines suggest is exciting this time of year. We've already seen how quickly September confidence can disappear at some programs. Season results : Brad Crawford (35-8 straight up, 25-17-1 ATS), Chris Hummer (35-8 straight up, 21–21-1 ATS) Y'all, it's time to celebrate Hummer moving back to .500 on the season ATS after a 6-4 week. We both took wins with Alabama's cruise at Mississippi State and North Carolina 's easy cover against Notre Dame during a rain-soaked game in Chapel Hill. Picking Miami to cover was shaky for two-and-a-half quarters before the Hurricanes laid it on the Tigers down the stretch to stay unbeaten. I whiffed on Michigan -5.5 at Minnesota . Kyle Whittingham has so much to fix in Year 1 with the Wolverines. All odds via FanDuel . No. 20 Iowa (+3.5) at Washington Hummer ( Iowa +3.5) : These are two of the better defenses in the Big Ten. Both Iowa and Washington are top 31 units nationally, and those defenses have carried both teams early. This game will be decided by which offense can manufacture the most points. Usually, I'd feel good about Washington doing so. After all, the Huskies have Demond Williams Jr . at QB. But he's really struggled this season and is turning the ball over far too often. Meanwhile, Iowa actually ranks ahead of Washington in yards per play (6.24 vs. 6.04). Iowa is the better team. It might actually have more playmakers. But I do think there's value with a Huskies cover, even at 3.5 points. … Iowa 21, Washington 20. Crawford (Iowa +3.5) : This is never an ideal situation as a ranked road underdog on a Friday night against a team coming off an emotional performance. The market's telling us something here. Washington quarterback Demond Williams Jr. will be the best player on the field, but I'm trusting the Hawkeyes' defense in this spot to fare better than it did last time out against Heisman favorite and my pick to win the award, Jeremiah Smith . Iowa can maintain its spot in the national rankings and march toward a potential 11-1 finish with a win, but I don't think there are going to be enough big plays to pull it out. ... Washington 23, Iowa 20. No. 7 Indiana (-9.5) at Nebraska Hummer ( Nebraska +9.5) : Once again, Nebraska is off to a hot start. And once again, it has a chance to change the program's narrative against a ranked Indiana team. Were the Huskers to pull the upset, it'd be their first win over an AP Top 25 team since 2016! And I do think there's value with the Huskers in this one. Would I like 10 points instead of 9.5? Absolutely. But the Huskers have looked good enough up front to hang with Indiana. And while the Hoosiers have still been largely dominant, they've shown some cracks in the trenches and at QB, where Josh Hoover has been good but a tad inconsistent. I'm not calling for an outright upset, but I do expect this game to be close. … Indiana 31, Nebraska 27. Crawford (Indiana -9.5) : Matt Rhule's last win over a ranked opponent came at Temple on Dec. 3, 2016, when his Owls beat Navy . Nebraska has lost nine such matchups under his watch and is staring at No. 10 this weekend against the Hoosiers. Both of these teams like to run the football, and they're doing it aggressively this fall, but Indiana's the more seasoned group in spotlight games -- and that matters here. For me, this comes down to trust, and the unbeaten Huskers need to show me they're capable of punching up a few weight classes before I'm ready to bet on them. Indiana covers in Lincoln in a game that should have the Hoosiers' full attention. ... Indiana 31, Nebraska 17. Texas A&M at No. 14 Missouri (-3.5) Hummer ( Missouri -3.5) : Texas A&M got a much-needed Arkansas boost of confidence a week ago. But I still have major concerns about the Aggies. Missouri's been an elite rush defense this season, which is bad news for A&M's run game, which has struggled. And if Missouri is taking away the run, it will be on Marcel Reed to make up for that. And based on what we've seen so far this season -- Reed ranks 77th nationally in QBR -- I don't have a lot of faith that he'll win that matchup. Throw in an A&M secondary that busts far too often, and I think the Tigers match up well in this one. … Missouri 27, Texas A&M 21. Crawford (Missouri -3.5) : The Tigers have looked focused all season, and they're two stops in the fourth quarter at Mississippi State away from being unbeaten and potentially ranked inside the top 10. Austin Simmons hasn't thrown an interception yet, and Jamal Roberts is running with steam in the backfield without Ahmad Hardy to assist. Missouri grabs everyone's attention with its destruction of Florida , while Texas A&M is simply trying to put together consecutive competitive performances in the SEC. I would've made this one closer to a touchdown, so there's value here. ... Missouri 34, Texas A&M 24. No. 1 Texas (-9.5) vs. Oklahoma Hummer ( Oklahoma +9.5) : The results in this game have been surprisingly volatile the last four years, with a trio of Texas blowouts in that stretch. But historically, this game is almost always close. Nine of the last 14 regular-season matchups were decided by a possession or fewer. I haven't seen anything so far this year that makes me feel differently about this game. I have more faith in Texas than Oklahoma. But both offenses have struggled, with Texas ranked 108th nationally in yards per play and Oklahoma 112th. At the risk of far oversimplifying a complicated game, I feel very confident in saying the QB who plays best, be it Texas' Arch Manning or Oklahoma's John Mateer , will win this game. I have slightly more faith in Manning at this point, so give me the Longhorns to win in a close one. … Texas 20, Oklahoma 17. Crawford (Texas -9.5) : This might not be the prettiest rivalry game in Dallas if you like big plays, but I just can't envision a reality in which Oklahoma scores enough points with this offense against Will Muschamp to warrant picking the cover here. Even with an extra week to sort out the struggles with the passing game under John Mateer, this Oklahoma team plays with little confidence when it has the football, and that means something against the No. 1 team in the country, hoping to tee off on the quarterback. The Sooners score on special teams for one of their two touchdowns. .. Texas 24, Oklahoma 14. No. 21 UCLA at No. 13 Oregon (-11.5) Hummer (Oregon -11.5) : This is the first big test for UCLA and Bob Chesney. Oregon has far better talent, and it'll be up to the staff to bridge that gap. Chesney is at least familiar with Oregon, having faced them a year ago at James Madison . Where I worry about UCLA's ability to hold up in this one is up front. The Bruins rank 91st nationally in pressure rate allowed in pass situations, while Oregon, despite a slow start, still has one of the nation's best defensive lines. And even if Dante Moore doesn't play, I'm confident Oregon's offense will move the football with Dylan Raiola . Give me the Ducks to make a statement after their bye week. … Oregon 38, UCLA 24. Crawford (UCLA +11.5) : Games with conference championship and CFP implications are here to stay the rest of the way for those inside the national rankings now that we're nearing the midseason point. The Bruins haven't lost yet under first-year coach Bob Chesney, but they're still flying under the radar nationally, and they prefer it that way. Dante Moore returned to practice Monday for the Ducks and could play this weekend. Oddsmakers are truly undervaluing UCLA here. And I think if this game were in Los Angeles, we're closer to a touchdown or so spread. ... Oregon 30, UCLA 24. No. 10 LSU (-10.5) at Kentucky Hummer ( LSU -10.5) : There's some interconnectivity with this game. Kentucky offensive coordinator Joe Sloan was LSU's play-caller a season ago, and several former Tigers players or signees came with him. This matchup will come down to a few key areas. First, can Kentucky's receivers make enough plays? Notre Dame quarterback transfer Kenny Minchey has been good this

However, the weather may take center stage with Tropical Storm Isaias potentially impacting the region ahead of Saturday's 7:30 p.m. EST kickoff. Alabama released a statement about the forecast ahead of Saturday's game, and it's possible that it could get moved if the storm becomes a major issue. For now, kickoff remains the same time on Saturday night. Information on Saturday’s Alabama football game vs. Georgia #RollTide | @AlabamaFTBL pic.twitter.com/KteQ9GgBZ6 Oddsmakers have already altered the odds for this game in a big way since they opened with Georgia favored by 2.5 points on Sunday. The total was originally 56.5 for this rivalry game, but that has come down considerably with the weather potentially playing a factor on Saturday. On Wednesday, DraftKings Sportsbook has the Crimson Tide set as 1.5-point favorites at home (a four-point swing in the odds) while the total has dropped four points all the way down to 52.5. This is a huge change for the opening numbers, and it's a sign that weather could impact how well these teams can move the ball on Saturday. Earlier this week, I shared why I'm taking Alabama and Keelon Russell to win this matchup, and I still lean that way even if Tropical Storm Isaias plays a factor: With Russell really turning a corner over the last few weeks, Alabama is now ninth in the country in EPA/Pass this season. Overall, the Crimson Tide are No. 2 in the country in net adjusted EPA/Play. There is an experience advantage for Georgia with Stockton under center, but this Alabama team has turned in four consecutive wins over quality teams in Kentucky, South Carolina, Florida State and Mississippi State. The Crimson Tide are No. 1 in the country in offensive success rate and No. 20 in defensive success rate, holding three of the four Power Four teams that they’ve played to 23 or fewer points. I think Alabama is going to be able to move the ball through the air against this Georgia team, and the Bulldogs haven’t been tested yet against an offense of this caliber. There's a chance the odds for this game could shift even more throughout the week, and the total would likely change if the game is pushed to a new time -- or even a different day -- to avoid this storm. For now, Alabama has a slight edge in what may be a low-scoring matchup on Saturday. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.headline: Alabama Given Strong Prediction vs Georgia in SEC Showdown
picks.blurb: Alabama Given Strong Prediction vs Georgia in SEC Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Guardians-White Sox updates Dodgers-Braves updates Eagles-Ravens trade grades OBJ signs with Vikes Messi's Argentina farewell Alabama Given Strong Prediction vs Georgia in SEC Showdown (Petre Thomas-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Wed, October 7, 2026 at 4:15 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The stage is set for the Alabama Crimson Tide to take on the Georgia Bulldogs this weekend in a massive SEC showdown. Alabama will be hosting the Bulldogs in the game, offering them a slight advantage coming into the contest. But this game will be anything but a bloodbath, with both sides desperately wanting to win. Each team enters this matchup with a record of 5-0, going 3-0 in SEC play so far this season. The two rivals have continuously given fans epic games over the years, and this matchup should be no different. Alabama comes in ranked No. 6 in the country, while Georgia is No. 2. For the Crimson Tide, they have a chance to take down one of the top teams in the nation at home, helping their own resume in the process. Entering the game, the matchup looks pretty even, with both teams having a real chance to take home the win. But according to ESPN's game predictor , Alabama has a slightly bigger opportunity to get the victory. Alabama has been given a 52.6 percent chance to take down Georgia, showing some of the slimmest of margins coming into the game. Part of why the Crimson Tide may be favored here is because the game is being played in Tuscaloosa. The Crimson Tide are very tough to beat at home, but Georgia is one of the few teams that has the talent to make it happen. Alabama will need to make sure that they bring their A-game into this matchup; otherwise, it could be a long night for everyone involved. Quarterback Keelon Russell is going to be tested in ways that he hasn't been so far this season, and he will need to prove that he can step up for the team. For Alabama to reach its big goals of winning a title this year, Russell is going to have to take on teams like Georgia while performing at a high level. But so far this year, Russell has passed all his tests with flying colors, entering his name into the Heisman Trophy conversation . If Russell can have another strong game against the Bulldogs, Alabama would likely be put in a good spot to grab the win at home. This is a measuring stick game for both teams, and the winner will have the upper hand to get into the College Football Playoff . Kickoff for this game will take place at 4:30 p.m. PT/7:30 p.m. ET from Bryant-Denny Stadium.

The Bulldogs haven't been tested much yet so far this year, but that's likely to change on Saturday against an explosive Crimson Tide offensive attack. Recently, college football media personality Josh Pate dropped a hot take in anticipation of the big matchup. "It's game of the year potential. It's not the end of the world for the loser. I think the winner, you can pencil into the playoffs at this point," said Pate, per the Rich Eisen Show, via ESPN College Football on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Indeed, winning this matchup would not only give either Alabama or Georgia a huge resume boost but also get them past arguably their toughest hurdle of the regular season, seemingly clearing the way for smooth sailing for the rest of the campaign. Last year, the Crimson Tide and Bulldogs squared off twice, with Alabama ending Georgia's home winning streak early in the season before the Bulldogs exacted revenge with a blowout win in the SEC Championship Game a few months later. Both teams saw their respective seasons come to an unceremonious end in the quarterfinal round of the college football playoff. It will certainly be interesting to see how the Bulldogs respond if they find themselves in a close game against Alabama on Saturday, as Georgia has yet to find themselves up against any real adversity so far this season. In any case, Alabama and Georgia are slated to kick things off on Saturday at 7:30 pm ET from Tuscaloosa. One of the biggest features of GameDay is the "celebrity guest picker," which is usually a celebrity or athlete with ties to the university hosting GameDay. This season's guest pickers have featured the likes of Morgan Freeman and Lainey Wilson. While it is anyone's guess, here are five options for the GameDay guest picker in Tuscaloosa this Saturday. Bryce Young, NFL quarterback Sep 20, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) looks to pass during the second quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The 2021 Heisman Trophy winner and 2023 No. 1 overall NFL draft pick, Bryce Young is one of the greatest quarterbacks in Alabama history. Young has been one of the top quarterbacks in the NFL this season. Young also has history with Georgia, having played against the Bulldogs in the 2021 SEC Championship Game in which he threw for 421 yards, as well as the 2021 CFP national championship. The Panthers have their bye week this upcoming weekend, which opens up the door schedule-wise for Young to potentially be the guest picker. Oba Femi, WWE superstar Oba Femi is introduced during WWE Friday Night SmackDown at Paycom Center in Oklahoma City, Friday, July 10, 2026. 28-year old WWE phenom Oba Femi, born Isaac Odugbesan , could be a strong option for ESPN if they opt to do some cross-promotion. ESPN currently owns the United States broadcast rights to WWE "premium live events" where Femi has become a fan-favorite with his patented entrance strut and powerful pro-wrestling style. Femi was a shot-put thrower at Alabama from 2019-22 where he was a two-time SEC Indoor conference champion. Femi toured the Alabama football facilities prior to the season, and was also featured on the "Paul Finebaum Show" at that time. Julio Jones, retired NFL wide receiver Dec 22, 2019; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Julio Jones (11) warms-up before their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jason Getz-USA TODAY Sports One of the greatest wide receivers of all time, Julio Jones holds a key spot in Alabama history as arguably the player that helped turn Alabama into a wide receiver factory. Having one of the premier players of the last couple decades would be a smart decision for GameDay. Jones also has history with Georgia as he went for five catches, 94 yards, and a touchdown in Alabama's 41-30 win over Georgia in the infamous Georgia blackout game in Athens during his freshman season in 2008. Jones is also set to feature in the Nick Saban documentary that ESPN is putting out, of which the first episode of is set to be released on Thursday . Justin Thomas, pro golfer Sep 27, 2026; Medinah, Illinois, USA; Justin Thomas of the U.S. Team watches his birdie putt on the 15th green after putting to win his match during the final round of the Presidents Cup. Mandatory Credit: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images If GameDay elects to go back to someone who has been the guest picker before, professional golfer Justin Thomas could be the choice. Thomas was previously the guest picker back in 2019 for the monstrous matchup between Alabama and LSU that season. Thomas was on the golf team at Alabama for two years, where he helped lead Alabama to a national championship in 2013, before turning pro. Thomas is a two-time winner of the PGA Championship and is currently the No. 26 ranked golfer in the world. Thomas recently competed for the United States in the 2026 President's Cup. Walker Hayes, singer Walker Hayes opens for Kane Brown during Brown’s Blessed & Free tour at Finley Stadium in Chattanooga, Tenn., on May 7, 2022. Hayes, who's song "Fancy Like" topped US Country charts in 2021 and 2022 is a native of Mobile, Alabama and is an Alabama fan. picks.headline: College Football Fans Clowning Josh Pate For His Alabama vs. Georgia 'Prediction'
picks.blurb: College Football Fans Clowning Josh Pate For His Alabama vs. Georgia 'Prediction' - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Guardians-White Sox updates Dodgers-Braves updates Eagles-Ravens trade grades OBJ signs with Vikes Messi's Argentina farewell Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There are a few kinds of "predictions" these days: There are well-thought out ones, there are "hot takes," and then there's "stating the obvious." College football analyst Josh Pate is getting called out for the latter. Appearing on The Rich Eisen Show this week, Pate talked with Eisen about the big Alabama-Georgia game and the stakes. Without missing a beat he declared that whoever wins the game is going to the College Football Playoff. "I think the winner, you can pencil into the playoffs at this point," Pate declared. Stating the Obvious Much? Given that Alabama and Georgia are respectively the toughest remaining opponents on their schedules, fans mocked Pate for stating such a seemingly obvious point: "Gee what a brilliant take. I wonder what his friends at FanDuel thinks of this," one user on X mocked. "He said pencil which implies it's still not a guarantee. Still refusing to make an actual prediction," another joked. "Really going out on a limb with this one Josh," a third joked. "What makes this even funnier is he said pencil not pen, bro still somehow found a way to not even commit to the most obvious take ever." "Josh is really going out on a limb with this one…" "Another scalding take from Josh Pate." Georgia coach Kirby Smart argues a call with the ref during the second half of the SEC Championship game against Alabama at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, on Saturday, Dec. 2, 2023. Alabama won 27-24. For what it's worth, there isn't much correlation between who wins the regular season matchup and who emerges as the SEC Champion or even the national champion. Last year alone we saw Alabama take down Georgia in the regular season, only for Georgia to destroy Alabama in a rematch in the SEC Championship Game. Both teams wound up getting knocked out in the same round of the CFP. There was a similar situation in 2022, when Alabama beat Georgia in the SEC Championship Game, only for Georgia to turn around and take down Alabama with the national title on the line.

away.blurb: It has been a week of checking the injury report for both the No. 2 Dawgs and Vanderbilt. Both starting Vanderbilt QB Jared Curtis and starting Georgia football RB Nate Frazier have been listed as "questionable" all week . ESPN reported Saturday morning that Curtis will be a game-time decision , and that he will likely try to play. That outlet further reported that there was "optimism" that Frazier would play against Vanderbilt. He has been out with what has been reported by ESPN with a rib injury. Vanderbilt coach Clark Lea said that Curtis has been trying to practice all week, but he's been limited. "He's banged up. He's not been able to be full-go in practice,” Lea said of Curtis. “So I think this has been about the injury report is there for a reason and we want to honor that. Questionable is the right marking for him right now. I'm hopeful. I think every day he's felt a little better and he's done a little more in practice. Certainly not ruling him out.” On ESPN's College Gameday, Nick Saban reiterated that the Dawgs are the "most complete team in the nation", but that UGA had limited upside because they are the No. 2 team in the country. away.headline: Vanderbilt QB Jared Curtis lands on injury report before Georgia showdown
away.blurb: Curtis landed in the “questionable” category on the injury report released by the SEC Wednesday. This could alter the Commodores’ offense once more under head coach Clark Lea. Vanderbilt football can deliver a massive statement Saturday by stunning No. 2 Georgia. Even after the Bulldogs’ epic beatdown of 2025 College Football Playoff team Oklahoma . But Vandy faces rolling without starting quarterback Jared Curtis for this showdown. Vandy previously turned to an RPO (Run Pass Option) offense with Diego Pavia. Including leaning into Pavia’s mobility to win games. That led to the 5-foot-9 QB rising as a Heisman Trophy finalist before losing to Indiana’s Fernando Mendoza. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Curtis arrived as a prized five-star signing for Lea and the Commodores. He became the first-ever five-star addition in the era of College Football Recruiting rankings. Curtis’s addition showed that Vanderbilt has grown popular among recruits in recent years, especially through Lea’s coaching. The big 6-foot-4 passer has flashed his potential; completing 63% of his throws while throwing four touchdowns. Curtis also has tossed three interceptions while starting in the last two games. Curtis does bring his own mobility too, adding 133 yards on 41 carries. But now once again, Georgia and head coach Kirby Smart may need to prepare for a second quarterback ahead of Saturday. Blaze Berlowitz could receive the nod here if Curtis can’t go. He’s a senior and shares a previous New Mexico State connection with Pavia. Berlowitz has tossed 178 yards so far this season. So a Vanderbilt upset could come with a different QB behind center. But such a feat would become the second-biggest win in program history. Ranking this with Vandy’s all-time stunner over No. 1 Alabama in Oct. 2024. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. away.headline: Georgia football vs. Vanderbilt injury report
away.blurb: One of the biggest impact players on the list for Georgia is Nate Frazier, who is dealing with a ribs injury. Frazier is questionable to play against the Commodores, and he missed last week's game against Oklahoma. The Bulldogs will, of course, be without outside linebacker Amaris Williams due to a torn ACL in his right knee. Williams is a spot on player, but the Bulldogs show to have plenty of depth to continue performing at a high level defensively. The other standout is outside linebacker Chase Linton, who is questionable due to a lower leg injury. He could return at any time. Linton has been considered week-to-week by Bulldogs coach Kirby Smart, but is almost ready to return. Freshman Safety Tyriq Green is ruled out and so is offensive linemen Marcus Harrison. Offensively, Isiah Canion is questionable for Saturday's game against Vanderbilt. Canion suffered a right leg injury early in the first quarter against the Arkansas Razorbacks on Sept. 19. Canion is expected to be a major part of the Bulldogs receiving game this season by bringing size to the outside. Keep an eye on when Canion may return. The Vanderbilt Commodores have six players on the SEC availability report. Four of the six are ruled out for Saturday's contest in Athens. All four of them are defensive players. The best defensive player out Saturday is Aaron Bryant who is out for the season with an ACL injury. Cornerback Jaylin Lackey, linebacker Jamison Curtis and defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson will be out also. Edge rusher Miles Capers is probable and freshman starting quarterback Jared Curtis is questionable. Out: Safety Tyriq Green (ankle) Out: Linebacker Amaris Williams (torn ACL) Out: Offensive Lineman Marcus Harrison Questionable: Running back Nate Frazier (ribs) Questionable: Wide receiver Isiah Canion Questionable: Linebacker Chase Linton (lower leg) Out: Defensive lineman Aaron Bryant Out: Defensive lineman Nikhil Jefferson Questionable: Quarterback Jared Curtis The Georgia Bulldogs will host the Vanderbilt Commodores Saturday, Oct. 3 at 12:45 p.m. ET. home.headline: Alabama Injury Updates for Jayvin James, Three More Players Ahead of Georgia Game
home.blurb: James left last the Sept. 26 home win over South Carolina early, as he sustained a lower extremity injury. Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer said last week that James was "very much questionable" for the Mississippi State game and was limited in practice throughout the week before being declared out. "Jayvin, we're optimistic that he can return this week," DeBoer said. "We'll see as the week goes on." "Tyrell is crazy athletic, has a lot of skill," DeBoer said. "And for him to get out there and get his feet underneath of him, I thought he did a nice job for his first, really, start, really from a volume standpoint, his most meaningful full reps. There's a high ceiling for him, for sure, and you can see that. "He's worked a couple of different positions, because throughout the year, throughout camp, we knew that he had that in him. But you're also trying to get him just settled in on one position and be really good at one spot. But got out there and did a nice job, and I thought both of them were integral to our success." "Jorden will still be out for quite a while yet still," DeBoer said. "There's a chance he can come back here, even in a regular season. But it will be a little bit yet." home.headline: Penn State week 5 injury report vs. Northwestern: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up
home.blurb: It’s still early in the year, but the injury bug has already bitten Penn State hard, forcing star wide receiver Koby Howard to miss the start of conference play. Howard’s absence was significant in the Nittany Lions Week 4 loss to Wisconsin, and he’ll be out again on Friday night when Matt Campbell’s team helps open the newly rebuilt Ryan Field at Northwestern. Daryus Dixson still listed as questionable on Thursday night availability report Dixson did not leave the Week 4 loss to the Badgers, but according to Campbell, who addressed Dixson’s health on Wednesday, he was “dinged up” just before halftime. Dixson was on the initial injury report on Tuesday night, listed as “questionable,” and held the same status on Thursday night when the availability report was released about 24 hours before kickoff in Evanston. The return of Alex Tatsch, who missed Week 1 as he ramped up from an injury he suffered preparing for the Pinstripe Bowl in December, has helped to fill the void left by Smith and Kooper Ebel, and Tony Rojas has been rock-solid at the second level of D’Anton Lynn’s defense. Dixson is seemingly the only player on Penn State’s roster whose status is uncertain heading into Friday night. Considering he played through the injury in the second half against Wisconsin, his outlook appears favorable, but that he wasn’t upgraded to “probable” raises a legitimate question about whether or not he’ll be ready to suit up against the Wildcats. Notable Northwestern injuries: Luke Dehnicke still doubtful While not ruled out, Northwestern has two starters listed as doubtful for Friday night, including its second-leading receiver: tight end Luke Dehnicke. Dehnicke caught seven passes for 140 yards against Indiana in Week 4, but was banged up and could miss Week 5. The Wildcats may also be without starting defensive back Braden Turner. Fellow starting DB Damon Walters is listed as questionable. home.blurb: Penn State DB questionable for Northwestern game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Penn State DB questionable for Northwestern game After last week's news surrounding the injury status of Koby Howard , Penn State fans could be forgiven for not wanting to hear anymore bad news. Now though, a pivotal defensive starter could miss some time as well. Sophomore cornerback Daryus Dixson apparently struggled with an injury during the Wisconsin game and is currently listed as questionable for the game against Northwestern . For Dixson, this could be a minor setback for what has been looking like a breakout season for the young corner. He recorded his first interception of the season last week and played the most snaps out of anyone on the defensive side of the ball. Most impressively, he has only allowed three receptions all season long, with the longest only being 16 yards. Against Buffalo, he also recorded a blocked field goal, proving his versatility and importance to the squad. While Dixson should be good to go should he miss the Northwestern game, others are not as lucky. Defensive end Max Granville suffered a season-ending injury in the first game of the season, his second in as many years. As for Koby Howard , no one knows when he will likely return, but to expect him to only miss a couple of games would be wishful thinking. Penn State fans can only hope this Dixson injury is the last of its kind this season.
